findings_could_not_do_first: NO FRAMES AT ALL, AND RULING W2 IS THEREFORE UNANSWERED. This is the biggest hole in the chunk and it is not a budget failure. The shared capture daemon took my requests, booted a browser three times (111 s, 165 s, 180 s — 456 s of boot) and returned `captures: 0, errors: 6`; every job dies with `closing browser: job timeout` because under the load that held all day the browser takes longer to BOOT than the job timer allows. Contention was 7 instances / 8.19 per core against a ceiling of 4.0 when I started and 11 instances / 10.82 per core when I finished. This is a fleet-wide condition. EVERY claim in my report is offline and derived from the game's own data and the renderer's own code; NOTHING in it should be read as a statement about how Thorn looks, and a person still has to go and look.

THE 48-FRAME SWEEP IS NOT DELIVERABLE ON THIS BOX and I did not pretend to attempt it. `tools/visual/w1-thorn-core12.sh` is committed: a 12-frame subset (4 yaws at noon plus 3 further times of day at the writ-house door, 2 roofline reads, the approach, and a 2-frame town-centre control), sized so a before AND an after both fit one budget. Both runs produced 0 frames.
THE THICKET (brief §6.5) IS NOT BUILT. It was the stretch item behind the quay and the roof, and the quay turned into a measurement problem worth more than the stretch.
MATERIAL RESPONSE STAYS n=0, as chunk 1 left it: pixel_metrics_valid is false on all 89 Morrowind plates, and I have no hardware frames either.

I REAPED MY OWN PIECE'S ORPHAN. Chunk 1's w1-thorn-sweep.sh was still alive and respawning captures from a shell whose session had ended (pid 2426), doubling the load on a daemon already failing every job. Killed by pid — my own piece's processes; no pkill, no sibling's browser touched.
findings: THE BRIEF'S LARGEST GAP RESTS ON A FALSE PREMISE, AND THIS IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THE CHUNK. Chunk 1 §6.2 prescribes giving Thorn a `tideline`, assuming its quay stands in water as Lilmoth's does. Measured from the engine's own WorldField (tools/render/w1-thorn-shoreline.mjs, committed, exits non-zero if the terrain field is constant): ground under both quay doors, the quay spawn, the approach and the Rotted Hall is 13.28 m at EVERY sample; waterAt().depth_m is 0.00 (band W0) at both quay doors; the nearest water is 30 m north of the writ-house door and 33 m north of the barge-hold door; the shoreline is a straight east-west line at z=938-939 across x=3790-3835; that water's surface is 14.60 m, i.e. 1.32 m ABOVE the ground the quay stands on, with 1.32 m of depth immediately at the edge and no shelving; and it is NOT TIDAL here — `tidal: false`, surface_y identical at all four tide phases. THE TIDEWRACK QUAY IS A QUAY 30 M INLAND OF A HARD-EDGED NON-TIDAL WATER BODY WHOSE SURFACE IS ABOVE ITS DOORSTEPS.

RULING T1 (mine, reversible): THORN GETS NO TIDELINE IN CHUNK 2. A tideline is a mark left by water on a thing the water touches; nothing at Thorn's quay touches water and no tide moves there, so a wet line and a drowned storey would be dressing a lie that would then be cited as proof the quay was fixed. WHAT WOULD OVERTURN IT: a terrain/water edit bringing the shore from z~938 to z~912 (about 25 m), after which `tideline: 1.32` is the MEASURED value (surface 14.60 minus quay ground 13.28) and the Lilmoth code path at exterior.js:1613 works against it unchanged. terrain.json and water.json both have other live claimants, so the number is handed over rather than acted on. This is the largest single improvement available to the opening of this game.

THERE IS ALSO NO CLIMB — brief §6.4 IS VOID AS WRITTEN. Sampled every 4 m from the writ-house door to the Rotted Hall door, terrain is 13.28 m at all ELEVEN points. The '~15% grade' is a comparison between the authored `door` y of the quay buildings (0) and of the town buildings (13.31), and buildSettlementExterior() does not use `door` y at all — it founds every building on groundY() at its own four corners. Both quay buildings are drawn on the same flat pad as the rest of the town. The only real verticality is the 1.32 m step up into the water at the shore.

roof.needle SHIPPED — THE FIRST NEW ROOF PROFILE THE GAME HAS HAD. Thorn's record promises 'black needle-wood laid in courses, which no other settlement uses' and the renderer had no such profile. It is a distinct SILHOUETTE, not a recoloured reed roof: steep (rise 0.62*min(w,d) against reed 0.38 and hip 0.30), a GABLE not a hip (open triangular end elevations), and a bristling ridge of projecting needle butts. Measured with the renderer's own planSettlement -> assignVariantSalts -> previewSilhouette: THORN GOES 2 -> 3 DISTINCT ROOF PROFILES (roof.needle x8, roof.reed x4, roof.hip x1 over 13 roofed buildings), tying Lilmoth for the most varied skyline in the province.

RULING E1's >=5 IS STILL NOT REACHABLE AND I DO NOT CLAIM IT. The kit now defines FOUR roof ids in total (hip, needle, reed, shell) against E1's five, so no grammar in the game can mix five. A kit gap, not a Thorn gap. 2 -> 3 is the honest step.

A CONSUMER-SEAM TRAP THAT WOULD HAVE PASSED EVERY COUNT IN THE TREE. exterior.js buildKitRoof() hard-codes the pitch per roof id AND passes `rise` explicitly, so a part's own `s.rise ?? ...` default never fires. A roof.needle registered at 0.62 and left out of that table renders at 0.30 — a slightly bristly hip — while previewSilhouette, which reads only the roof ID, still counts a fourth distinct profile everywhere. Exactly RULES rule 5's 'a correct, instrumented model that nothing in the running world reads'. Fixed at the table and commented as the change's real consumer seam.

DELETE-THE-FIX DONE, CONTROL WENT RED. On a hard-linked control clone with kits.js and exterior.js reverted to base commit f434730c: thorn falls back to 2 profiles, roof.reed x13 + roof.hip x5, BYTE-IDENTICAL to chunk 1's reported baseline, and the kit falls back to 3 roof ids; the other seven towns are identical in both arms, which is the proof the change is scoped to Thorn.

A TRAP WORTH RECORDING: MY FIRST DELETE-THE-FIX ARM CAME BACK GREEN — the control did NOT go red — because `git show HEAD:` no longer held the 'before'. The orchestrator bank had already carried my uncommitted edit into HEAD (commit 9aac1cbb) minutes earlier, which is exactly what RULES rule 17 says the bank does. On a tree banked every few minutes, HEAD IS NOT YOUR BASELINE; your session's base commit is. I re-ran against f434730c and the control went red properly.

THE INSTRUMENT CROSS-VALIDATES AGAINST CHUNK 1. tools/render/w1-thorn-roof-census.mjs was written independently (chunk 1's lived in a scratchpad and is gone) and reproduces chunk 1's profile counts EXACTLY on all seven towns I did not touch. It carries chunk 1's own mistake as a permanent negative control — a constant seed collapses every town to 1 profile — and EXITS NON-ZERO if the two arms ever agree. Note it counts ROOFED records only (a `structure` returns early in buildBuilding() and draws no roof), which is why its Thorn row says 13 where chunk 1's said 18; the profile counts are unaffected.

THE TIDEWRACK LANDING BUILT, AND FIVE OF ITS SIX PARTS ARE REUSE. tidewrack-quay held 2 buildings and no props at all. Six structures now sit AT THE MEASURED WATERLINE (z=935-941, x=3796-3820) rather than on dry ground where they would be untrue: The Tide Courses (tho_tide_mark <- lil_tide_mark), The Tidewrack Piles (tho_pile_cluster <- lil_pile_cluster), The Landing Stage (tho_stilt_platform <- lil_stilt_platform), The Boom Chain (tho_boom_chain <- lil_boom_chain), The Writ Quay (tho_silt_quay <- sou_silt_quay), and one NEW part, The Moored Barge (tho_moored_barge) — REF-A19's own subject, a longboat with a green-and-white striped sail, and the thing that says a barge came in, which is how the player got here.

THE REUSE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT COPY-PASTE — directive §3's 'make this structural, not a hope'. THORN_QUAY_REUSE is a table binding Thorn's ids to the NEIGHBOURS' BUILDERS through kitMesh(), so there is exactly one definition of a driven pile in the build and a fix reaches both shores; what differs is that kitMesh is handed Thorn's palette, so the same piles come out in thornmarsh's swatch. Four lines instead of five new part builders. Exported as thornQuayReuse().

CONSUMPTION PROVED WITH THREE CONTROLS, ALL RED (tools/render/w1-thorn-quay-consumption.mjs). All six parts are declared in thorn.json, bound in STRUCTURE_KIT, buildable by kitMesh() and placed by planSettlement() at the intended coordinates. Perturbation 1: undeclare the mesh -> all six resolve to null (6/6). Perturbation 2: the committed semantic=false arm (the old hash rule) -> 5 of 6 bind to something different; the moored barge happens to hash to itself, reported rather than hidden. Perturbation 3: kitBuildable('tho_a_part_that_does_not_exist') -> false. buildNamedStructure() THROWS if a structure's mesh cannot be built, so a green run is also proof these six records cannot break Thorn's exterior build.

THE REGION QUESTION IS SETTLED AND IT WAS A HARNESS ARTEFACT, NOT A WORLD DEFECT — resolved in the first ten minutes as instructed. WorldField.regionAt(), the position-derived lookup that actually drives ground, fog and flora, returns `thornmarsh` at ALL of the quay spawn, both quay doors, the approach and the town centre. The harness's `western-rootlands` comes from sim.env.region, a cached field NOTHING in the engine updates from player position (INVENTORY V15, open, owned by W1-02/W1-30F, already diagnosed by W1-30E-KIT-DEFECTS which records region_at_player from getTerrainAt instead). Nothing is being dressed as Lilmoth's region. I checked before fixing and did NOT touch the field — it is another piece's.

BOARD ANCHOR RE-ROUTED IN THE GENERATOR ONLY. docs/art-direction/build-board.mjs routed thorn to REF-A3, whose five plates are ALL square crops (0 of 5 composition-valid), so Thorn's rows could never be set whatever the town looked like; the old basis also cited `spiral-palisade`, which is not one of architecture.json's nine grammars at all. Re-routed to REF-A19 (n=6, Morrowind's own waterside settlement), with the reasoning and the reversal condition written into the file. I did NOT touch board.json or ART.md — they are generated and W1-30K's, and this lands in the generator so the next regeneration picks it up. stormhold is n=0 for the same reason and is DELIBERATELY not fixed here; it needs its own judgement, not a copy of this one.

PUBLISHED FOR REUSE BY THE OTHER SEVEN TOWNS: roof.needle (a fourth roof profile any grammar can mix); the THORN_QUAY_REUSE pattern (one town's ids bound to another's builders, per-town materials); w1-thorn-roof-census.mjs (Ruling E1's number for every settlement, with a control that fails the tool rather than the town); w1-thorn-shoreline.mjs (where the water is relative to any stand, for any town on a shore).

SHARED-TREE CHECKS GREEN on the changed tree: check-data (587 indexed files, 115/115 interiors big enough for their rooms, 408 NPC records, every settlement resolves) and check-content (551 quest resolutions, 1108 authored topic/actor pairs) both exit 0.
overlap_note: kits.js and exterior.js are shared with several live pieces (ownership.mjs reports 3 and 4); build-board.mjs is W1-30K's. Declared deliberately rather than left to read as a collision. Every edit is additive and narrowly scoped: one new roof part in the roof section, GRAMMARS.thorn's roofs/roofMix, one arm in buildKitRoof's pitch table, a THORN_QUAY_REUSE block after EXT_KIT, six STRUCTURE_KIT rows, six appended records in thorn.json, and one anchor line in build-board.mjs. Landed with --paths only.
next_step: IN ORDER. (1) MOVE THE WATERLINE TO THE QUAY — terrain.json/water.json, about 25 m of shore — then reverse Ruling T1 and set `tideline: 1.32` on GRAMMARS.thorn. Everything else on that quay waits on it and it is the largest single improvement available to the opening of the game. (2) RUN tools/visual/w1-thorn-core12.sh TWICE, once against f434730c and once against now, AND LOOK AT THE PICTURES — Ruling W2 is owed and no offline number substitutes for it; do it when contention is under the ceiling, because the daemon's job timer is shorter than its browser boot under load. (3) Two more roof profiles if Ruling E1's >=5 is to mean anything for any town: four ids is the ceiling today and three settlements are still on one profile. (4) The thicket — thornmarsh already declares depth:'hook-arch-thickets' and nothing closes the sky over Thorn's streets. (5) stormhold's board anchor, n=0 for the same reason Thorn's was.
